title: M1 assessment layer: formative checks, lightweight auto-checker, and capstone rubric
context: PLAN.md v0.2 promotes the lightweight auto-checker out of 'post-MVP / M4+ backlog' and mandates it from M1: formative checks per lesson, a Rosalind-style expected-output/answer checker introduced in M1, a capstone rubric, and an optional diagnostic pre-test. This is distinct from the advanced autograder in bioinfo-zero-autograde-401 (M4+, mastery / diagnostic pre-tests at depth). This M1 task delivers the minimal viable assessment layer: simple expected-output checks that run in CI and locally, per-lesson formative questions (not just full exercises), and a capstone rubric document so self-paced learners have verifiable checkpoints from the start of the curriculum.
objective: Deliver the M1 assessment layer: (1) a lightweight auto-checker tool (Rosalind-style expected-output/answer checks) that runs in CI and locally for both R and Python tracks, introduced in M1; (2) at least one formative check per M1 lesson wired to the auto-checker; (3) a capstone rubric document (for M3); and (4) an optional diagnostic pre-test for the 'from zero' entry floor (validates a learner truly starts from zero). The auto-checker must not leak solutions prematurely.
acceptanceCriteria: A lightweight auto-checker tool (tools/checker/ or similar) checks learner outputs against expected results for at least the M1 tabular and visualisation lessons in both R and Python tracks.
The auto-checker runs in CI (every commit) and can be run locally by a learner without leaking hidden solutions.
Each M1 lesson (setup-101, tabular-102, viz-103, stats-104) includes at least one formative check wired to the auto-checker with a checkable expected output.
A capstone rubric document (docs/capstone-rubric.md) is committed with clear, self-assessable criteria for the M3 capstone (capstone-302).
An optional diagnostic pre-test (docs/diagnostic-pretest.md or a short runnable quiz) is included to help learners validate they start at the declared 'never-opened-terminal' entry-skill floor.
Reviewed by Technical + Pedagogy reviewers; tool code licensed MIT, rubric/pretest licensed CC-BY-4.0.
